caption:
Peace begins where you decide what is enough.

Name your enough in one area today.

From "The 14-Day Clarity Reset." Type the word "Think" and I'll send you the link.

#clarity #seneca #simpleliving #contentment #mindset

text: “It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.”
He was one of the richest men in Rome.
He still wrote about the danger of wanting more.
Wanting is a moving target.
Reach it, and the goalpost shifts.
Clarity includes knowing your enough.
Enough time. Enough things. Enough proof.
Try naming it for one area of life.
Write the number or the condition.
Then notice when you cross it.
Stop. Enjoy it. Let it count.
Peace is not having everything.
It is knowing when you have enough.
In one area of your life, what would be enough?
This is the thread behind the book *The 14-Day Clarity Reset*.
Subtract the craving to see what is left.
Name your enough.
*Then rest in it.*

caption:
Your thinking deserves the same care as your body.

Give your mind a quiet half hour today.

From "The Science of Learning Your Inner Speech." Type the word "Think" and I'll send you the link.

#innerspeech #pascal #thinking #mindfulness #selfawareness

text: “All our dignity consists, then, in thought.”
Pascal called us thinking reeds.
Fragile, yet able to understand our own fragility.
That is a quiet kind of dignity.
It does not depend on status.
Thought is also a daily habit.
It can be neglected or tended.
Give it a regular place.
A walk. A page. A quiet half hour.
Treat your own thinking as worth protecting.
It is the one thing no one can do for you.
Small attention to your mind adds up.
When did you last give your thinking real, undistracted time?
This is the thread behind the book *The Science of Learning Your Inner Speech*.
Give your inner voice room to think well.
Protect your thinking.
*It is yours.*

caption:
A clear mistake teaches more than a vague maybe.

Write one view in a sentence and test it this week.

From "Learn To Think For Yourself." Type the word "Think" and I'll send you the link.

#thinkforyourself #francisbacon #criticalthinking #learning #mindset

text: “Truth emerges more readily from error than from confusion.”
A wrong answer can be corrected.
A vague one cannot.
Many of us avoid committing to a view.
We stay fuzzy to stay safe.
Bacon suggests the opposite.
State it clearly, so it can be tested.
Write your best guess in one sentence.
Then look for what would prove it wrong.
Being wrong becomes useful.
It points to what to fix.
Clear errors teach faster than cloudy caution.
What is one view you could state clearly this week and test?
This is the thread behind the book *Learn To Think For Yourself*.
Thinking for yourself means committing, then checking.
State it.
*Test it.*

caption:
Anger often costs more than whatever caused it.

Take one breath before your next reaction.

From "The 14-Day Clarity Reset." Type the word "Think" and I'll send you the link.

#clarity #marcusaurelius #stoicism #calm #mindset

text: “How much more grievous are the consequences of anger than the causes of it.”
The cause may be small.
A comment. A delay. A tone of voice.
The anger it sparks can last for days.
It costs sleep, focus and kindness.
Weigh the two before you react.
Is the cause worth the consequence?
Give yourself one breath first.
One sentence: *what actually happened?*
Often the answer is smaller than the feeling.
That gap is where choice lives.
You cannot stop every spark.
You can decide how much fire it gets.
What small thing has your anger been carrying for too long?
This is the thread behind the book *The 14-Day Clarity Reset*.
Daily steps to meet frustration with clear thinking.
Pause once.
*Then choose.*
